title: Build CI result reuse, routing, and after-measurement (ci-routing 4-7)
summary: Implement build-plan items 4–7 of docs/design/ci-routing.md: per-SHA CI result reuse with local fallback, routing by job kind per the 3.2 table, a before/after comparison in `xtask walltime`, and the closing docs. Audience is the owner and the verifier, who judge by tests that fail without the mechanism and by measured, labeled numbers.

defaults_applied.how: All new logic and tests in Rust.
New modules have tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check SHA mismatch, missing, and red behavior by running tests, not file existence.
Missing or stale CI results never yield verified; the job blocks if local fallback cannot run.
Docs label unmeasured numbers as estimates.
Four items kept as separable steps in one change; item 7 docs last.
Measurement compares wall time with equal checks run.
Reuse rules are enforced by tests that fail without them.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Item 6 needs N≈20 real post-build jobs, which cannot exist inside this change. I assume the job builds the comparison tooling (xtask walltime after/compare mode against the #117 baseline) and records the after numbers only if records exist, otherwise states plainly that they are not yet measured.
'Baseline from #117' means the output/doc of the baseline job (docs/design/ci-routing-baseline.md); I did not check what #117 contains.
Result reuse lives in athena-core (checks.rs, verify.rs, gh.rs) with wiring in athena-cli; Athena, not the verifier, fetches the CI record, and the verifier command set stays unchanged (design 3.3).
The design review is still open; the owner's request overrides it, as it did for items 2 and 3.
Not checked in detail: the exact current code structure of checks, verify and gh; paths are the likely ones.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test --locked`: tests show a CI result whose SHA differs from the candidate's is ignored, a missing/cancelled/timed-out result triggers the local fallback run, a red result fails the check without fallback, and a stale record never marks a job verified.
Run `cargo test --locked`: tests show one run of fmt/clippy/test per SHA is reused by the verifier input and by Athena's check step, so the same SHA is not checked twice.

Run `cargo test --locked`: routing tests cover each job kind in design 3.2 (code, tests, docs, design, config, build, study); docs-only skips fmt and clippy but not test; a workflow-file change in the candidate forces local run; a job with no kind takes the config all-checks path.

Run `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- walltime` on fixture records: it outputs before/after medians and p90 by job kind, flags fewer than 20 jobs, and flags a regression when the after median exceeds the baseline.
The verifier's allowed command list in athena.toml is unchanged, and the verifier input carries the CI record (SHA, run address, per-step conclusions).

docs/design/ci-routing.md section 10 marks items 4–7 built or partly built, naming what is not done; any after-measurement number is either measured from records with the command shown or stated as not yet measured.
README and CHANGELOG describe the routing and result reuse in a way a new reader can follow, and a decisions entry records the call.

out_of_scope: Widening the verifier's command set or giving it network/gh access
Recording the design review verdict or marking the design accepted
Self-hosted builders or local compiler caches (alternatives F, G)
Fabricating after-measurement numbers when too few post-build jobs exist
departures: Request bundles four build-plan items (core logic, routing, tooling, docs) across many crates, so cost, time and risk exceed the reference; the after measurement also depends on data that may not exist.
